# draftably

> draftably is a text format for diagrams. A `.draft` file lists boxes, groups and connections, one statement per line, and automatic layout draws them. A free public renderer at https://draftably.dev/api turns the source into an image URL, with no install and no account.

This file has everything an agent needs to draw a diagram: the recipe below, the syntax, and complete examples. To work on `.draft` files in a repository, install the CLI and its agent skill (see Docs). To show or edit diagrams in a web app, start with [Choose how to embed](https://draftably.dev/docs/embed/).

## Draw a diagram with no install

No CLI, no API key, no encoder to write. The service checks the source and hands back short links.

1. Write the source. This is a complete architecture diagram: two titled groups, boxes with a smaller detail line (`\n`), labeled arrows inside and across the groups, and a note.

```text
diagram "Share a snapshot"
subtitle "The owner approves; teammates read a copy until it expires"

group hub "Private hub" color=blue
node owner "Owner" shape=pill in=hub
node live "Account data\nlive, per account" in=hub
node agent "Agent\nbuilds and publishes" in=hub

group shared "Shared" color=teal
node team "Teammates" shape=pill in=shared
node copy "Snapshot\none published copy" in=shared

edge approve owner -> agent "approves preview"
edge export live -> agent "snapshot"
edge publish agent -> copy "publish"
edge read team -> copy "read if unexpired"
note "Only the owner can withdraw the copy." near=copy side=right

layout root flow direction=right
```

2. Send it as plain text to `https://draftably.dev/api/link`, as the request body:

```sh
curl --data-binary @diagram.draft https://draftably.dev/api/link
```

   From a tool that can only GET, open `https://draftably.dev/api/link?code=<source>` with the source percent-encoded (see "Share a short link" below). When the source draws, the answer is `200` and text with the image and editor links:

```text
png: https://draftably.dev/api/d/<id>.png
svg: https://draftably.dev/api/d/<id>.svg
edit: https://draftably.dev/d/<id>
markdown: ![Diagram](https://draftably.dev/api/d/<id>.png)
```

   Add `?format=json` for `{"id", "png", "svg", "edit", "diagnostics"}`. Long image links for the source above: [SVG](https://draftably.dev/api/svg/pako:eJxdkkFu3DAMRfc-BcF10wsUDpATpECynA1tMRYBDSlI1Dhz-8K2PEm6Evz1KX4-Oggtha6Ab5EKA0FVyjWa41Db5OKJAd8jg63KBSjnYjeuf8CZrldyrlCYAhDMlu_Q1CWBOPBnlsIVh2Ep1jLENgH-LXIj5-0DYbZkZZxS40EtnA3wdTsQaqTMY5aUQHSMbTpMSW4M-DLP1tQhkNNFN-0X5C3doeOPElpYHfBlOy46NUmhAmmA3KYkNXJ9-HvWuqEIHUk4kzpTOl7cRgd8PwH8H_YoP6w7FHzrTC9qyo--Yb_FbyUDh4VPxh3I0_M5wckecuGb8IqHnT-zFT_IfJm_1ribes9--_Tcg3W5m_ZF7sM9DLskH9D0WGjAQc0Z8FXTHfzxX8yksIrHUGjd5a38N4IylXF_qkrgscgSfRgS3a05FDOHj2QrBCk8u5h2xz8eEOnC), [PNG](https://draftably.dev/api/png/pako:eJxdkkFu3DAMRfc-BcF10wsUDpATpECynA1tMRYBDSlI1Dhz-8K2PEm6Evz1KX4-Oggtha6Ab5EKA0FVyjWa41Db5OKJAd8jg63KBSjnYjeuf8CZrldyrlCYAhDMlu_Q1CWBOPBnlsIVh2Ep1jLENgH-LXIj5-0DYbZkZZxS40EtnA3wdTsQaqTMY5aUQHSMbTpMSW4M-DLP1tQhkNNFN-0X5C3doeOPElpYHfBlOy46NUmhAmmA3KYkNXJ9-HvWuqEIHUk4kzpTOl7cRgd8PwH8H_YoP6w7FHzrTC9qyo--Yb_FbyUDh4VPxh3I0_M5wckecuGb8IqHnT-zFT_IfJm_1ribes9--_Tcg3W5m_ZF7sM9DLskH9D0WGjAQc0Z8FXTHfzxX8yksIrHUGjd5a38N4IylXF_qkrgscgSfRgS3a05FDOHj2QrBCk8u5h2xz8eEOnC), [editor](https://draftably.dev/play#s=XZJBbtwwDEX3PgXBddMLFA6QE6RAspwNbTEWAQ0pSNQ4c_vCtjxJuhL89Sl-PjoILYWugG-RCgNBVco1muNQ2-TiiQHfI4OtygUo52I3rn_Ama5Xcq5QmAIQzJbv0NQlgTjwZ5bCFYdhKdYyxDYB_i1yI-ftA2G2ZGWcUuNBLZwN8HU7EGqkzGOWlEB0jG06TEluDPgyz9bUIZDTRTftF-Qt3aHjjxJaWB3wZTsuOjVJoQJpgNymJDVyffh71rqhCB1JOJM6Uzpe3EYHfD8B_B_2KD-sOxR860wvasqPvmG_xW8lA4eFT8YdyNPzOcHJHnLhm_CKh50_sxU_yHyZv9a4m3rPfvv03IN1uZv2Re7DPQy7JB_Q9FhowEHNGfBV0x388V_MpLCKx1Bo3eWt_DeCMpVxf6pK4LHIEn0YEt2tORQzh49kKwQpPLuYdsc_).

3. Fix what it names. A bad source gets `400` and no links. The error names the line, quotes its text, and usually says the fix:

```text
error: line 5: hub is a soft group, so it has no layout of its own. Use frame=box, or set the layout of the container around it.
> layout hub row gap=24
```

   Fix that line and send it again. `info` and `warning` lines come back after the links on a good source too; they name arrows that run against the reading order, notes that cover the drawing, and colors without a legend. Act on them before you share.

4. Look at the PNG before you share it. A diagram can be valid and still read badly: a label that wraps, a box that pulls the eye from the main path. The image shows what the diagnostics can't.

5. Revise. Send the edited source to `/link` again for new links. The `edit` link opens the diagram in the editor; for a long image URL, change `/svg/` or `/png/` to `/edit/`.

Options on `/link` and the image URLs: `?scheme=dark`, `?type=mermaid|draftably`; `?scale=1|2|3|4` for PNG (default 2). Mermaid flowcharts, sequences, gantt charts and timelines also work. Free use is 60 new drawings a minute per address and 30 new links; an image drawn before and a link made before are free. The service refuses sources over 64 KB, and an image URL over 8 KB.

To build a long image URL yourself, it is `https://draftably.dev/api/svg/<encoded>` (or `/png/`), where `<encoded>` is base64url of the UTF-8 source with no `=` padding, or `pako:` + base64url(zlib(source)) for a shorter URL. It stores nothing. A bad source then returns `400` and an image that names the line; the same message is in the `X-Draftably-Error` header. The PNG carries its source, so dropping it on https://draftably.dev also opens it for editing.

### Rules that trip agents up

- One `layout` line per scope. A `frame=soft` or `frame=none` group takes no `layout`, `near` or `pin` of its own; use `frame=box` (the default) to lay out its members.
- An `edge` needs its own ID before the ends: `edge go a -> b "label"`.
- `\n` in a label starts a smaller detail line. Keep the first line to two to four words.
- Members of a group stack in the order you declare them. Declare the source of an arrow before its target, or `/link` reports an arrow that runs up.
- Colors are names from the list below, not hex values.
- Try the automatic layout before you reach for `pin` or `size`. Change `direction=`, the declaration order, or `order` first.

### What makes the drawing good

- Pick the one path the reader must follow, and give it the clearest labels. Keep inputs and context secondary.
- Label every arrow with what it means: a call (`"approves preview"`) or what moves (`"snapshot"`). An unlabeled arrow can mean either.
- Put a rule on the path it governs (`"read if unexpired"`), not in the text of a box.
- Draw boundaries honestly: a system the service only reads goes outside the group, with the arrow labeled.

## Syntax

One statement per line; indentation means nothing. Strings use double quotes; `\n` in a label starts a smaller detail line. IDs match `[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*`. Comments start with `#` or `//`.

- `diagram "Title"` and `subtitle "One-line takeaway"`: optional, drawn above the diagram.
- `node id "Label"`: a box. Options: `in=group`, `color=`, `shape=box|pill|circle|diamond|text`.
- `group id "Label"`: a container. Options: `in=group` (groups nest), `color=`.
- `edge id from -> to "label"`: a connection with its own ID. The label is optional. `kind=async` draws it dashed.
- `legend color "meaning"` and `legend line dashed "meaning"`: the key under the diagram.
- `note "text" near=id side=below|above|left|right`: a sentence beside an object.
- Colors: `slate`, `stone`, `blue`, `sky`, `teal`, `mint`, `green`, `amber`, `orange`, `red`, `rose`, `violet`.
- Layout, one line per scope (`root` or a group ID):
  - `layout root flow gap=48`: boxes and arrows, the default. Add `direction=right` or `direction=down`, and `fit=slide` for a slide-shaped drawing.
  - `layout group row gap=24` or `layout group column gap=24`: a group's members in a line.
  - `layout root lanes`: each top-level group is a swim lane.
  - `layout root sequence`: nodes are participants; each `edge` is one message, in file order.
- Sequence diagrams: `message=call` (the sender waits), `message=send` (it does not), `answers=id` (a reply to message `id`), `action id participant "label"` (work on one lifeline), and `phase id "label" m1 m2 ...` (a band around consecutive messages; it can't skip one).

A flow diagram:

```text
diagram "Checkout"
group shop "Shop" color=blue
node web "Web app" in=shop
node api "API" in=shop
node db "Postgres" color=violet
edge order web -> api "place order"
edge save api -> db "insert"
edge mail api -> web "receipt" kind=async
layout root flow direction=right
```

A sequence diagram:

```text
diagram "Load a profile"
subtitle "The API reads the profile and returns it"

node browser "Browser"
node api "API"
node db "Database"

edge ask browser -> api "GET /profile" message=call
edge read api -> db "select profile" message=call
edge row db -> api "profile row" answers=read
edge reply api -> browser "200 JSON" answers=ask

phase fetch "Fetch" ask read row reply

layout root sequence
```

For every statement and option, read the [language guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/byronwall/draftably/main/skills/draftably/SKILL.md) (plain Markdown; its Syntax section is the part that matters without the CLI).

## Connect over MCP

The MCP server at `https://draftably.dev/mcp` (Streamable HTTP) has the tools `render_diagram`, `validate_diagram`, `convert_mermaid`, `image_url` and `language_guide`. Rendering spends credits from a free account (1,000 a month).

- ChatGPT: Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced settings, turn on Developer mode. Create a connector with URL `https://draftably.dev/mcp` and OAuth. Sign in by email and press Allow.
- claude.ai and Claude Desktop: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector with URL `https://draftably.dev/mcp`. Sign in by email and press Allow.
- Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http draftably https://draftably.dev/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer dft_..."`, with a key from https://draftably.dev/account
- Codex: `codex mcp add draftably --url https://draftably.dev/mcp --bearer-token-env-var DRAFTABLY_API_KEY`
- Cursor and other JSON configs: `{"mcpServers": {"draftably": {"type": "http", "url": "https://draftably.dev/mcp", "headers": {"Authorization": "Bearer dft_..."}}}}`

- [Content on nodes](https://draftably.dev/docs/content-on-nodes/): your own markup on a node with `data-draft-slot` and `data-draft-input`
- [Camera and geometry](https://draftably.dev/docs/camera-and-geometry/): `fit`, `reveal`, `getCamera`, `setCamera` and `geometry()`
- [Events and status](https://draftably.dev/docs/events-and-status/): every `draft-<name>` event, which element sends it, its prop name in each framework, and the diagnostic codes
- [Theming](https://draftably.dev/docs/theming/): dark pages, frame colors and editor colors
- [Server rendering and strict CSP](https://draftably.dev/docs/server-rendering/): `renderSvg` fallbacks and a complete nonce policy
- [API reference](https://draftably.dev/docs/api-reference/): every export, element property, viewer option and handle method
- [Performance](https://draftably.dev/docs/performance/): what a page loads, many diagrams, and main-thread mode
- [Troubleshooting](https://draftably.dev/docs/troubleshooting/): each symptom and its fix
- [Upgrade to 0.4](https://draftably.dev/docs/upgrade/): every breaking change, with code before and after

## Share a short link

The render service at https://draftably.dev/api turns a source into a short image link with one GET, so agents that can only browse can make one:

1. Write the diagram source.
2. Open `https://draftably.dev/api/link?code=<source>`, with the source percent-encoded. Encode all of it: a raw `#` ends the URL, `&` starts a new parameter and `+` reads as a space, so write them as `%23`, `%26` and `%2B`. Example: `https://draftably.dev/api/link?code=node%20a%20%22Hello%22%0Anode%20b%20%22World%22%0Aedge%20e%20a%20-%3E%20b`
3. The answer is text with `png`, `svg` and `edit` URLs, such as `https://draftably.dev/api/d/<id>.png`. A source that doesn't draw returns `400` and the line to fix.
4. To show the image, copy the returned `markdown` line; it uses the SVG when a PNG would be too large. To let someone edit it, share the `edit` URL, which opens the diagram on draftably.dev.

The same source always gets the same link. For a shorter request, send base64url of the source, or `pako:` + base64url(zlib(source)), in the path: `/link/<encoded>`. `POST https://draftably.dev/api/link` with the source as the body, or `POST /v1/share` with `{"code": "..."}`, takes large sources. `/png?code=<source>` and `/png/<encoded>` are long image URLs that store nothing.
